description:
## Goal

An already-queued matching message must win before a zero-duration receive timeout on interpreter, JIT, and AOT. `after 0` means do not wait when the current mailbox has no match; it does not mean skip the current mailbox.

## Proven defect

At the accepted fz-kdt.27 boundary `aed4bc247`, this production program prints 42 through the backend interpreter and 0 through JIT:

```fz
fn main() do
  send(self(), :go)
  result = receive do
    :go -> 42
  after
    0 -> 0
  end
  dbg(result)
end
```

Both executions exit successfully, so this is a semantic ordering divergence rather than a crash. A receive-capture fixture during fz-tfn.64 exposed it; changing the timeout to 1000 makes the native path accept the message and independently proves the new physical capture ABI.

Existing ticket and open-PR searches found no live owner. Closed fz-1ah.13 repaired divergent return-flow continuation sealing and is not this mailbox-versus-timeout ordering defect.

## Correct model

Receive first probes the current mailbox in arrival order through the existing shared pattern plan. A matching message is removed and its outcome runs. Nonmatching messages remain queued. Only after the current mailbox has no match may timeout policy decide whether to wait, schedule a timer, or immediately run an `after 0` branch.

The timeout and message paths consume the same receive state/continuation authority. Do not add a zero-only pattern exception, sleep, retry, polling loop, duplicate mailbox scan, alternate queue, or interpreter-specific behavior. Timer readiness is transient scheduling state, not semantic authority.

## TDD signal

Pin the minimal reproduction through interpreter, JIT, and standalone AOT. Add controls for:

- queued matching message with `after 0`: message wins;
- empty mailbox with `after 0`: timeout wins;
- queued nonmatching messages with `after 0`: timeout wins and unmatched messages remain queued;
- a nonmatching message before a matching message: selective receive finds the match without reordering the survivor;
- multiple matching messages: first matching arrival wins;
- message and timeout becoming ready at the scheduler boundary: the already-present mailbox state is examined before timeout;
- captured receive arms and timeout arms retain their existing ABI and values;
- unchanged compilation reuses retained products and deterministic artifacts.

Use production runtime/receive telemetry if the deciding scan/order is not otherwise observable. Assert semantic results and exact mailbox effects, not wall-clock duration.

## Strategy and deletion

Trace the native receive entry from scheduler wakeup to the first decision that selects timeout without probing the current mailbox. Move the ordering authority to the existing receive state transition so the invalid ordering is unrepresentable. Share the corrected transition across JIT/AOT and preserve interpreter agreement.

Delete any superseded timeout-first branch, duplicate readiness bookkeeping, temporary probe, and construction fixture. Update receive/scheduler documentation if the current ordering contract is absent or false. Run focused receive/scheduler/runtime tests, all three doors, full library and fixture gates, formatting, check, strict Clippy, deterministic artifact/work proof, and a fresh ticket-scoped cold adversarial review. One ticket, one commit, one close.

## Ordering

This defect is independent of fz-tfn.64 and does not block its pattern/outcome cutover. It is a low-priority correctness obligation of the epic and blocks only fz-tfn.60, the final semantic-fidelity and debris proof.
title: Make prequeued messages win before receive after zero
